question: Do useful donor episodes exist despite the globally accumulated mixture favoring the parent, and does an ideal per-episode reset pay before finite arithmetic and package costs?
mechanism: Read-only instrumentation around the sealed Adapter. No donor, prediction, arithmetic, update or population change. Compare every original probability hash and all1015 complete adapter-state boundaries before accepting attribution.
measurements: Pure expert versus parent ideal bit savings for every episode
Episode start, donor start and length in explicit WRT coordinates
First Q63 parent saturation, number of exits, last changed Q16 bit
Sum of positive episode gains, hindsight routing cost after one selector bit per episode
Analytic ideal equal-prior reset gain log2((1+2^g)/2) per episode; no Q63 or finite-archive guarantee
selection: One fixed previously measured development trace, no tuning or confirmation. Preserve all episodes, including negative and partial episodes.
decision: If ideal reset fails to improve on parent, do not implement that reset as a proposed remedy. If profitable episodes exist but resets lose, a causal opportunity/calibration diagnosis is required before any selector. If reset passes, separately freeze its exact arithmetic implementation and controls; no native promotion from ideal costs.
execution: Two synthetic attribution tests first, then publish source/input bindings and verify fresh resource admission before one retained-trace attribution. CPU3 only, exclusive output path, explicit process timeout and inherited rlimits. Preserve HORIZON and MIDAS. No native inference, architecture change, installation or corpus extension.
failure_classification: Trajectory/hash/coordinate or aggregation mismatch is invalid evidence; resource stop is execution failure; nonpositive ideal reset is a scoped rejection of resetting this unchanged episode mixture, not every edit expert.
